content:
Rain Maki, Circulation Manager | November 5, 2026

image courtesy of UW-Platteville Helios Program

For the first two months of the semester, around 600 first year students, with the help of English teachers and Helios co-directors, Amanda Tucker and Katie Kalish, in the Helios program collaborated on creating a new cryptid creature for the campus. The activity was structured to give participants an opportunity to collaborate, be creative, and strengthen their sense of belonging at Platteville.

The creation of the Driftling was done over several sessions, each one refining the look of the creature, where it would live, and how it would act around the student body. During these sessions, the students would also speculate on what the Driftling would say about the community, as cryptids reflect something about the community they come from. The students settled on an outside presence peering in, wanting to belong, but scared to be truthful with those around it. In the end, the habitat of the Driftling was decided to be the basement and sub basement of Ottensman Hall, and takes the form of a deer in order to observe students from afar without arousing suspicion. Students on the project also speculated that in the basement, the Driftling would keep lots of old school supplies, with a guardian bringing it more as offerings. It would do this, not to be malicious, but to feel connected to the students, despite being too scared to show itself to them. The students on the projects also did not name the creature.

The Driftling was named by Dr. Tucker, as a nod to the driftless region between loneliness and wanting to belong. When the creature was finalized, the students did send a description of the Driftling to Mike Bass, cryptid illustrator and author of the book “Frightful Folklore of North America.” Bass then sent back two illustrations of the creature, one of it in the Capstian Hall in the Markee, as a normal buck, the other is of the creature in its “true form.” Still having the form of a deer, but now also with sixteen black eyes, and elongated hands and fingers as antlers with each one of the finger’s nails painted black.
